items.title: [cpu_backend] Add stride-1 max pool (separable NEON) kernel
items.body:
## Dependency of the PR None. Independent of other PRs. ## Commits to be reviewed in this PR
[cpu_backend] Extract maxpool2d_s1 NEON kernel from pooling2d_layer
Moves the stride-1 max pool implementation out of `pooling2d_layer.cpp` into the `cpu_backend` dispatch layer, following the same pattern as `depthwise_conv2d`. **Algorithm:** Replaces the naive O(ph×pw×n) 2D scan with a separable two-pass approach: - **Row pass** – `tmp[ih][w] = 1D sliding max` over a pw-wide horizontal window - **Col pass** – `out[oh][w] = 1D sliding max` over a ph-tall vertical window of `tmp` Each pass uses NEON `vmaxq_f32` (fp32, 4-wide) / `vmaxq_f16` (fp16, 8-wide) over the full spatial dimension, guarded by `#ifdef __ARM_NEON`. x86 and non-NEON ARM fall back to scalar via `__fallback_maxpool2d_s1`. The temporary buffer (one `[Hi×Wi]` plane) fits in L1/L2 for typical SPPF feature maps. **Self evaluation:** 1. Build test: [X]Passed [ ]Failed [ ]Skipped 2. Run test: [X]Passed [ ]Failed [ ]Skipped Signed-off-by: SeungHui Lee
[cpu_backend] Add default-throw impl + unittest for maxpool2d_s1
Adds the required out-of-line `ComputeOps::maxpool2d_s1_fp32/fp16` default-throw bodies to `compute_ops.cpp` (same pattern as every other virtual op). Adds three GTest cases to `unittest_nntrainer_fallback` that compare `__fallback_maxpool2d_s1_fp32` against a naive reference loop across: - 3×3 kernel, no padding (7×7 input → 5×5 output) - 3×3 kernel, same-padding (8×8 → 8×8) - 5×5 kernel, same-padding (13×13 → 13×13) All element-wise comparisons use `EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ`. **Self evaluation:** 1. Build test: [X]Passed [ ]Failed [ ]Skipped 2. Run test: [X]Passed [ ]Failed [ ]Skipped Signed-off-by: SeungHui Lee
[cleanup] Apply clang-format-14 to feat/opt-pooling2d changed files
Applied `clang-format-14` to all files modified in this branch. **Self evaluation:** 1. Build test: [X]Passed [ ]Failed [ ]Skipped 2. Run test: [X]Passed [ ]Failed [ ]Skipped Signed-off-by: SeungHui Lee
### Summary - Extracts `maxpool2d_s1_fp32/fp16` into the `cpu_backend` dispatch layer (ARM NEON / x86 scalar / fallback) - Replaces O(ph×pw×n) naive 2D max scan with separable O((ph+pw)×n) two-pass NEON algorithm - fp32: `vmaxq_f32` (4-wide), fp16: `vmaxq_f16` (8-wide), scalar fallback for x86/non-NEON - Adds `ComputeOps` default-throw stubs and 3 correctness unit tests ### Validation Measured on **Galaxy S25 Ultra (Snapdragon 8 Elite, 8 threads, YOLOv11m q40-fp16)**: | Layer | Before | After | Speedup | |-------|--------|-------|---------| | `pooling2d` (SPPF 5×5 max pool) | 14.2 ms | 1.6 ms | **9.1×** | Detections bit-identical to baseline. 2.5× fewer NEON ops for 5×5 kernel (10 positions vs 25). items.title: [CausalLM] Add XLM-RoBERTa encoder-only model with differential tests
items.body:
## Summary

This PR adds XLM-RoBERTa (`XLMRobertaForMaskedLM`) as an encoder-only
embedding model in the CausalLM application, along with two prerequisite
bug fixes in shared layers and a differential test suite.

### What changed

**Bug fixes (prerequisite)**

- `EmbeddingLayer::save` – removed a silent bypass that wrote raw FP32
  bytes for `height==1` embedding tables (e.g. `token_type_embeddings`
  with `type_vocab_size=1`) instead of quantizing them. This corrupted
  Q4_0 binaries whenever an encoder model had a single-row embedding
  table. Callers now control dtype selection explicitly via the
  `dtype_map` in `quantize.cpp`.

- `MHACoreLayer::incremental_forwarding` – changed `to >= max_timestep`
  to `to > max_timestep` so a sequence whose final write position exactly
  equals the KV-cache capacity (a common case for encoder-only models
  that process up to `max_seq_len` tokens) is no longer incorrectly
  rejected.

- `main.cpp`, `quantize.cpp` – applied clang-format-14 to fix lambda
  argument line-break style in `XLMRobertaForMaskedLM` factory registration.

**New model: XLMRobertaForMaskedLM**

Inherits `BertTransformer`; concrete differences from BERT:

| Parameter | BERT | XLM-RoBERTa |
|---|---|---|
| `type_vocab_size` | 2 | 1 |
| `layer_norm_eps` | 1e-12 | 1e-5 |
| `encode()` return | last hidden state | last hidden state (no pooling) |
| HF `architectures` key | `BertForMaskedLM` | `XLMRobertaForMaskedLM` / `XLMRobertaModel` |

Wired into `main.cpp` (inference), `quantize.cpp` (Q4_0 quantization),
and both model/application `meson.build` files.

**Test suite**

A tiny fixture (2 layers, 4 heads, hidden=64, vocab=32, `type_vocab_size=1`)
generated from HuggingFace `XLMRobertaModel` validates:

- `FP32MatchesHFReference` – raw last-hidden-state within atol=2e-2 and
  cosine similarity ≥ 0.999 of the HF reference.
- `Q40CloseToFP32Reference` – Q4_0 quantized output within atol=0.1 and
  cosine similarity ≥ 0.99; skips automatically when `NNTR_QUANTIZE_BIN`
  is not set.

## Test plan

- [ ] Build on Linux x86: `meson setup builddir && ninja -C builddir`
- [ ] Run unit tests: `./builddir/Applications/CausalLM/unittest_causallm_models --gtest_filter="TinyXLMRobertaDifferentialTest.*"`
- [ ] Run with `NNTR_QUANTIZE_BIN` set to confirm Q4_0 test exercises the quantize path
- [ ] Confirm existing embedding-model tests (MultilingualTinyBert, DebertaV2, etc.) are unaffected

> **Draft PR** — CI/test verification pending before merge.

items.title: Support gliner2-multi-v1 model
items.body:
## What
Let's support the `gliner2-multi-v2 model` for Named Entity Recognition (NER). 
- This model utilizes `microsoft/mdeberta-v3-base` as its back-bone.
- It introduces a specialized architecture (GLiNER) for span representation and entity counting.

## How
We need to implement the DebertaV2 architecture and GLiNER-specific modules.

### 1. DebertaV2 Backbone
- The core difference from standard `BERT` is the Disentangled Attention mechanism.
- We need to implement `DebertaAttentionLayer` which handles Content-to-Content(c2c), Content-to-Position(c2p), and Position-to-Content(p2c) attention scores separately.
- Relative positional embeddings shoud be handled dynamically.

### 2. GLiNER Specialized Layers
- **SpanRepLayer** : Aggregates token embeddings into span repreentations by concatenating start and end token projection.
- **CountLSTMLayer** : Predicts the number of entities in the text using a sequence modeling approach.


## TODO
- [ ] DebertV2 Backbone encoder Implementation
  - [ ] Implement DebertaLayer and DebertaV2 model](https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/pull/3773)
- [ ] GLiNER Specific modules
  - [ ] Implement `SpanRepLayer`
  - [ ] Implemnet `CountLSTMLayer`


### FYI
- hugging face - [gliner2-multi-v1](https://huggingface.co/fastino/gliner2-multi-v1)
- transformers - [deberta_v2](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/tree/main/src/transformers/models/deberta_v2)

<details>

<summary>model structure</summary>

```console
============================================================
🧠 Model Configuration
============================================================
Encoder model      : microsoft/mdeberta-v3-base
Counting layer     : count_lstm
Token pooling      : first
============================================================

GLiNER2(
  (encoder): DebertaV2Model(
    (embeddings): DebertaV2Embeddings(
      (word_embeddings): Embedding(250112, 768, padding_idx=0)
      (LayerNorm): LayerNorm((768,), eps=1e-07, elementwise_affine=True)
      (dropout): Dropout(p=0.1, inplace=False)
    )
    (encoder): DebertaV2Encoder(
      (layer): ModuleList(
        (0-11): 12 x DebertaV2Layer(
          (attention): DebertaV2Attention(
            (self): DisentangledSelfAttention(
              (query_proj): Linear(in_features=768, out_features=768, bias=True)
              (key_proj): Linear(in_features=768, out_features=768, bias=True)
              (value_proj): Linear(in_features=768, out_features=768, bias=True)
              (pos_dropout): Dropout(p=0.1, inplace=False)
              (dropout): Dropout(p=0.1, inplace=False)
            )
            (output): DebertaV2SelfOutput(
              (dense): Linear(in_features=768, out_features=768, bias=True)
              (LayerNorm): LayerNorm((768,), eps=1e-07, elementwise_affine=True)
              (dropout): Dropout(p=0.1, inplace=False)
            )
          )
          (intermediate): DebertaV2Intermediate(
            (dense): Linear(in_features=768, out_features=3072, bias=True)
            (intermediate_act_fn): GELUActivation()
          )
          (output): DebertaV2Output(
            (dense): Linear(in_features=3072, out_features=768, bias=True)
            (LayerNorm): LayerNorm((768,), eps=1e-07, elementwise_affine=True)
            (dropout): Dropout(p=0.1, inplace=False)
          )
        )
      )
      (rel_embeddings): Embedding(512, 768)
      (LayerNorm): LayerNorm((768,), eps=1e-07, elementwise_affine=True)
    )
  )

  (span_rep): SpanRepLayer(
    (span_rep_layer): SpanMarkerV0(
      (project_start): Sequential(
        (0): Linear(in_features=768, out_features=3072, bias=True)
        (1): ReLU()
        (2): Dropout(p=0.1, inplace=False)
        (3): Linear(in_features=3072, out_features=768, bias=True)
      )
      (project_end): Sequential(
        (0): Linear(in_features=768, out_features=3072, bias=True)
        (1): ReLU()
        (2): Dropout(p=0.1, inplace=False)
        (3): Linear(in_features=3072, out_features=768, bias=True)
      )
      (out_project): Sequential(
        (0): Linear(in_features=1536, out_features=3072, bias=True)
        (1): ReLU()
        (2): Dropout(p=0.1, inplace=False)
        (3): Linear(in_features=3072, out_features=768, bias=True)
      )
    )
  )
  (classifier): Sequential(
    (0): Linear(in_features=768, out_features=1536, bias=True)
    (1): ReLU()
    (2): Linear(in_features=1536, out_features=1, bias=True)
  )
  (count_pred): Sequential(
    (0): Linear(in_features=768, out_features=1536, bias=True)
    (1): ReLU()
    (2): Linear(in_features=1536, out_features=20, bias=True)
  )
  (count_embed): CountLSTM(
    (pos_embedding): Embedding(20, 768)
    (gru): GRU(768, 768)
    (projector): Sequential(
      (0): Linear(in_features=1536, out_features=3072, bias=True)
      (1): ReLU()
      (2): Linear(in_features=3072, out_features=768, bias=True)
    )
  )
)
```
</details>

items.title: Make padding zero cost
items.body:
Lets make padding zero cost for pooling , convolution or any future layers.
Lets say convolution needs padding, then the input tensor `In_c` allocated for this must  be tensor of padded size (input shape  + padded). The previous layer which treats `In_c` as its output tensor will have the same memory but a tensor with different shape and stride (which does not include padding). In this way, once the previous layer fills in the output, convolution layer automatically receives padded input without any extra cost.

The same optimization will be done for pooling and for backwarding as well.
This not only reduces the cost of the memcopy of the padding but also the temporary memory allocation overhead and its corresponding rise in peak memory is also removed.

items.title: [Issue] Enhancing `incremental_forwarding` interface
items.body:
Currently, `incremental_forwarding` is used in nntrainer to support various XLM types. However, its current design is limited to a single-input / fixed-range scenario, which assumes that all layers share the same from and to values.

As mentioned in #3779 , we need to support cases where a single layer receives multiple inputs from different layers, each requiring unique from and to values determined at runtime. Consequently, we must update incremental_forwarding to support the layer-by-layer relay of these values.

Main Requirements:
- To address this, we must satisfy the following requirements:

1. Support for Multi-batch Input
The system must handle multiple from and to values passed from the API level (e.g., in model.h) to accommodate multi-batch scenarios.

```C++
virtual std::vector<float *> incremental_inference(
    unsigned int batch, 
    const std::vector<float *>& input, 
    const std::vector<float *>& label, 
    unsigned int init_seq_len, 
    const std::vector<unsigned int> from, 
    const std::vector<unsigned int> to, 
    bool output_hidden_state = false
) = 0;
```

2. Layer-by-Layer Value Propagation
We must ensure that from and to values are correctly relayed to subsequent layers, guaranteeing that values for multiple layers are handled properly.

Proposed LayerNode Signature:

```C++
std::pair<std::vector<unsigned int>, std::vector<unsigned int>> 
LayerNode::incremental_forwarding(
    std::vector<unsigned int> from, 
    std::vector<unsigned int> to, 
    bool training
);
```

Logic in neuralnet.cpp:

```C++
std::tie(from, to) = node->incremental_forwarding(from, to, training);
```
Implementation Note

While the simple case involves passing a single pair of vectors, we must extend this logic to handle multi-input layers by managing how from and to vectors are appended or mapped for each specific input source.

items.title: [ Wait for #4309 ] [opencl] Quantized GEMM on the GPU: the int8 x int4 kernel, its tensor views and host dispatch
items.body:
The fully-connected weights of a transformer are the bulk of its parameters and,
quantized to four bits, the bulk of its arithmetic. This puts that multiply on
the GPU: an int8-activation by channel-wise-int4-weight GEMM that never
dequantizes, plus the tensor views and host dispatch it needs.

Nine commits, in dependency order:

1. `ClTensorView` / `ClTensorBackingPool` — read a tensor's device memory as an
   image2d, and keep one such view per weight. Internal helpers, not installed.
2. Fill in `DeviceCaps` at OpenCL context init. The struct has existed since the
   execution-plan change; nothing probed it until now, and the GEMM below is its
   first caller. The two fields whose real signal is a compiler trait rather than
   a CL query are keyed on the vendor id, with the reasoning written at the site.
3. `enqueueSVMMap` gains a non-blocking mode, defaulted off, for the case where
   the next reader is the GPU rather than the host. It also stops discarding the
   event out-parameter it accepted.
4. The kernels: two device families of the same algorithm (image-sampling, and a
   buffer-load variant for runtimes whose compiler rejects integer-coordinate
   `read_imageui`), a GEMV path for single-row decode and a tiled path with a
   valid-row store guard otherwise, and the activation quantizers whose row sums
   let the zero-point correction fold into the GEMM epilogue.
5. `ClComputeOps::fc` routes through it. The entry point declines rather than
   throws, so a weight it cannot take still reaches the host dot or `dotCl`.
6-8. Three corrections to the above, kept separate because each documents a
   non-obvious property: the plain-page drop is opt-in and names its live
   consumer; the image view is released by its owner only, not twice; and the
   shared-quant cache is scoped to one forward pass rather than keyed on a
   pointer the tensor pool will reuse.

Verified on an Intel Xe iGPU, gcc-13 `-Werror`, tests on, transformer on. Without
OpenCL: 43/43 test targets green with fp16 off; with fp16 on, only the two
pre-existing `compute_kcaches` overload failures. With OpenCL and fp16 on every
suite was run against an identical build of the base commit, and the failing name
sets are byte-identical: `unittest_layers` 1190/1193 both sides (all nine
`FullyConnectedGPU` goldens green), `unittest_opencl_kernels_blas` 28/29 both,
`unittest_cl_residency` 9/9, `unittest_attention_kernels_cl` green, and the two
pre-existing kernel suites unchanged at 16/27 and 1/11 — a device resource
ceiling on both sides, not a regression.

A review-response round adds seven more commits: the four changes requested
against the first head (the per-forward memset dropped, the cached weight's two
device buffers given a real owner, the shared-quant cache refused where no pass
boundary is provable, and the SVM map's async flag appended after the event
rather than inserted before it), the smaller corrections that came with them,
three bring-up tuning knobs retired, and -- closing the gap this description
used to disclose -- `unittest_opencl_kernels_v8c`, which checks the kernel
against the host dot over the same QS4CX weight at three shapes, checks that an
unsupported shape is declined rather than thrown, and pins the shared-quant
cache at both boundary cases. It skips rather than fails where no device takes
the dispatch.

+1157 -41 · this PR 8 / 18 / +4545 -8. Whole stack 55 commits, 133 files,

items.title: Feature/flash attention opencl
items.body:
# Flash Attention OpenCL Optimization Summary

## Performance Trajectory (FP16 Prefill, 512×512, GQA 16→8)

| Stage | FP16 Prefill | FP32 Prefill | Key Change |
|-------|-------------|-------------|------------|
| Baseline | 194 ms | 42 ms | Row-by-row kernel, two-pass softmax |
| Phase 2 | 69 ms | 152 ms ⚠️ | Tiled GEMM + online softmax |
| Phase 3 | 45 ms | 42 ms | FP16 local mem + FP32 accumulation |
| Phase 4 | 50 ms | 38 ms | GQA grouping (NCOLS2=1 default) |
| Phase 5 | 50 ms | 40 ms | Adaptive ncols1 + vectorized access |
| Phase 6 | 50 ms | 39 ms | Decode kernel infrastructure |
| **Adreno kernel** | **32 ms** | **39 ms** | Parallel softmax + half4 + FP16 FMA |

**Cumulative**: FP16 194→32 ms (**6.1× faster**), FP32 42→39 ms (1.1× faster)

---

## Optimizations KEPT ✅

| # | Optimization | Phase | Impact | Commit |
|---|-------------|-------|--------|--------|
| 1 | Separate prefill/decode dispatch | Phase 1 | Enables all subsequent | `cd56ca59` |
| 2 | Tiled GEMM + online softmax | Phase 2 | FP16 2.8× faster (194→69ms) | `f8f74254` |
| 3 | FP16 local memory + FP32 accumulation | Phase 3 | FP16 1.53× faster (69→45ms) | `f8f74254` |
| 4 | GQA grouping (NCOLS2=1 default) | Phase 4 | Infrastructure, no regression | `22451fd4` |
| 5 | Adaptive ncols1 + vectorized access | Phase 5 | Infrastructure, no regression | `f35c6d5a` |
| 6 | Decode kernel + KV_max skip | Phase 6 | Infrastructure for decode | `51473c9a` |
| 7 | Parallel online softmax (FP32) | Phase A | Works for FP32 tiled kernel | `5ca8aa1f` |
| 8 | **Adreno FP16 prefill kernel** | Phase A-Adreno | **1.37× faster** (44→32ms) | `6264454a` |
| 9 | Zero-fill removal + nrows_kv bounds | Round 2 | Code cleanup, no regression | `c88ae76a` |
| 10 | half8 + dot() intrinsic | L4-3 | No improvement, no regression | `16b250f3` |
| 11 | Eliminate redundant Q·K in decode | L4-4 | 30-40% decode improvement | `385fcd40` |
| 12 | Adreno-specific decode kernel | L4-5 | Decode now runs on GPU | `385fcd40` |
| 13 | VKQ float4 FMA | L4-6 | 4-6% prefill improvement | `16b250f3` |
| 14 | Fix decode local memory waste | L4-8 | 768 bytes saved | `385fcd40` |
| 15 | native_exp() in decode | L4-11 | 1-2% decode improvement | `16b250f3` |

---

## Optimizations REVERTED ❌

| # | Optimization | Phase | Impact | Root Cause | Commit |
|---|-------------|-------|--------|------------|--------|
| 1 | **Bank conflict padding** (HEAD_DIM+4) | Phase B | **50% regression** (32→48ms) | Adreno handles bank conflicts in HW; padding wastes local mem | `c88ae76a` |
| 2 | **NBATCH_FA=16** (reduce local mem) | Phase C | **9% regression** (32→35ms) | 2× more KV iterations outweigh occupancy gain | `c88ae76a` |
| 3 | **Scale fusion into Q load** | Phase E | **9% regression** (32→35ms) | half4 multiply overhead > single FP32 multiply savings | `c88ae76a` |
| 4 | **Double buffering** (async_work_group_copy) | Phase F | **6% regression** (32→34ms) | Scalar DMA slower than half4 vectorized loads | `c88ae76a` |
| 5 | **Per-WI Q row processing** (v2 kernel) | L4-1 | **15.7× slower** (33→520ms) | Register pressure + poor coalescing on Adreno | `a808ddeb` |
| 6 | **Image objects for K/V** (texture cache) | L4-2 | **11.5% slower** | Image creation overhead + TP cache too small | `a808ddeb` |
| 7 | **GQA-2 NCOLS2=2** (dispatch fusion) | L4-14 | **23% regression** (30.6→37.8ms) | Local mem 20→24 KB, occupancy 3→2 WGs/CU | — |
| 8 | **GQA-2 NCOLS1=2,NCOLS2=2** | L4-15 | **Neutral/+6%** (30.6→32.4ms) | 2× more WGs offset dispatch savings | — |
| 9 | **Larger tiles** (32×32, 64×64) | L4-16 | **Predicted regression** | 32×32=45KB→1 WG/CU; 64×64=89KB→exceeds 64KB | — |

---

## Key Insight: Occupancy Is the Binding Constraint

On Adreno 840 (64 KB local memory/CU), the current configuration is the sweet spot:

```
NCOLS1=4, NBATCH_FA=32 → ~20.5 KB local mem → 3 WGs/CU
```

**Every change that reduces occupancy from 3→2 WGs/CU causes 9-23% regression**, regardless of the data reuse benefit. This was validated across 5 independent tests (Phase B, Phase C, L4-14, Opt 9, NCOLS1=8).

---

## Not Yet Started ⬜

| # | Optimization | Expected Impact | Risk |
|---|-------------|----------------|------|
| L4-7 | Fuse VKQ correction into accumulation | 2-3% | Low |
| L4-9 | Parallelize reduction kernel head_dim loop | 5-10% | Very Low |
| L4-10 | Reduce reduction buffer with sub-groups | 960 B saved | Low |
| L4-12 | Eliminate softmax correction branch | 0-1% | Medium |
| L4-13 | KV cache layout interleaving | Uncertain | High |
| Phase D | Optimize work-group size selection | Uncertain | Low |
| Phase 7 | Sub-group/wave matrix multiply | 2-5× | Requires Intel/AMD GPU |

---

## Profiling on Adreno 840 GPU

### Test Configuration

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Device | Qualcomm Adreno 840 (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3) |
| Test | FP16 prefill, 512×512, GQA-2 (16Q/8KV), head_dim=128 |
| Kernel | `flash_attention_prefill_fp16_adreno.cl` |
| Work-group size | 128 work-items |
| Local memory per WG | ~20.5 KB |
| Occupancy | 3 WGs/CU (64 KB local memory) |
| Dispatches | 2 (one per Q head group in GQA-2) |

### Profiling Method

OpenCL event profiling (`CL_PROFILING_COMMAND_START/END`) measures per-dispatch execution time and queue submission time. The test runs 100 iterations with 2 dispatches each.

### Profiling Results (Baseline: NCOLS1=4, NCOLS2=1)

```
Per-dispatch execution: ~15.3 ms (consistent across 200+ samples)
Queue submission overhead: ~300-370 µs per dispatch
Total GPU per iteration: ~30.6 ms (2 dispatches × ~15.3 ms)
GPU 100-run average: 36 ms (includes CPU↔GPU transfers)
CPU single run: 534 ms (nntrainer CPU reference)
CPU 100-run average: 1056 ms
Speedup: 4.9× (single), 29.3× (average vs nntrainer CPU)
MSE Error: 3.24e-14, Cosine Similarity: 1.0
```

### Profiling Observations

1. **Consistent per-dispatch time**: ~15.3 ms with <2% variance — no thermal throttling
2. **Queue overhead is small**: ~350 µs / 15.3 ms = 2.3% of dispatch time
3. **Two dispatches for GQA-2**: Each dispatch processes 8 Q heads (one per KV head group)
4. **No pipeline overlap**: SVM sync after each iteration forces GPU→CPU round-trip

---

## Why nntrainer GPU Is Slower Than llama.cpp CPU

### Head-to-Head Comparison (512×512, GQA-2, head_dim=128)

| Metric | llama.cpp CPU | nntrainer GPU (Adreno) | Ratio |
|--------|--------------|----------------------|-------|
| **Prefill time** | **8.80 ms** | **32.0 ms** | **CPU 3.6× faster** |
| **Decode time** | **0.09 ms** | **1.678 ms** | **CPU 18.6× faster** |
| Precision | Q=FP32, K/V=FP16 | Q/K/V=FP16 | GPU has advantage (less bandwidth) |
| Threads | 8 (OpenMP) | 1 GPU | CPU uses all big cores |
| Algorithm | Tiled GEMM (Q_TILE=64) | Tiled GEMM (NCOLS1=4) | CPU has 16× larger Q tile |
| Synchronization | None (single-threaded per tile) | 256+ barriers per WG | GPU barrier overhead dominant |
| Peak utilization | **79% of FP32 peak** | **7.5% of FP16 peak** | GPU severely underutilized |

### Thread Scaling: CPU Already Saturates at 1 Thread for GQA-2

| OMP_NUM_THREADS | Prefill 512×512 (ms) | Speedup vs 1 thread |
|----------------|---------------------|---------------------|
| 1 | 8.85 | 1.00× |
| 2 | 8.91 | 0.99× |
| 4 | 9.12 | 0.97× |
| 8 | 8.80 | 1.01× |

**Key finding**: The CPU tiled GEMM path already saturates memory bandwidth with a single core for GQA-2 prefill. The 8.80 ms time is effectively a single-core result — the GPU comparison is already fair.

### Root Cause: 5 Compounding Factors

#### Factor 1: Barrier Overhead (Dominant Bottleneck)

The cooperative processing model (128 work-items sharing 4 Q rows) requires barriers at every step:

- Per KV tile: 4 Q rows × (max_reduce + sum_reduce + state_update + VKQ_correction) = 16 barriers (with sub-groups)
- 16 KV tile iterations: **256 barriers total per work-group**
- Each barrier: ~20-50 cycles (all 128 work-items must synchronize)
- **Estimated barrier overhead**: ~30-40% of kernel time

llama.cpp CPU has **zero barriers** — each thread processes its Q tile independently.

#### Factor 2: Small Q Tile Size

| | nntrainer GPU | llama.cpp CPU |
|--|-------------|--------------|
| Q tile size | 4 rows (NCOLS1=4) | 64 rows (Q_TILE_SZ=64) |
| Compute per tile iteration | 64K FLOP | 1024K FLOP |
| Overhead-to-compute ratio | High | Low |
| K/V reuse per load | 4 Q rows share | 64 Q rows share |

NCOLS1=4 was chosen because NCOLS1=8 causes 15% regression (occupancy drops 3→2 WGs/CU). The cooperative model doesn't scale to larger Q tiles on Adreno.

#### Factor 3: Low GPU Utilization (7.5% of Peak)

**Roofline analysis** (FP16 prefill 512×512):
- Total FLOP: 1.07 GFLOP
- Total memory: 6 MB (Q+K+V read + output write)
- Arithmetic intensity: 178 FLOP/byte → **compute-bound**
- Adreno 840 FP16 peak: ~4.5 TFLOP/s
- Theoretical minimum: 1.07 GFLOP / 4.5 TFLOP/s = **0.24 ms**
- Actual: 32 ms → **7.5% of peak FP16 utilization**

**CPU comparison**:
- CPU FP32 peak: ~96 GFLOP/s (8 cores × NEON)
- Theoretical minimum: 1.07 GFLOP / 96 GFLOP/s = **11.1 ms**
- Actual: 8.80 ms → **79% of peak FP32 utilization**

The CPU achieves 10.5× better utilization than the GPU.

#### Factor 4: Decode Is Memory-Bound + Launch Overhead

For decode (1×512):
- Arithmetic intensity: 1.05 FLOP/byte — **extremely memory-bound**
- GPU: 2 kernel dispatches (decode + reduce) + SVM allocation + SVM sync = ~1.678 ms
- CPU: Single function call, K/V in L2 cache = 0.09 ms
- GPU effective bandwidth: 1.25 GB/s (2% of 60 GB/s)
- CPU effective bandwidth: 23.3 GB/s (39% of 60 GB/s)

#### Factor 5: SVM Sync Overhead

nntrainer calls `enqueueSVMMap()` after each kernel dispatch, forcing GPU→CPU synchronization. This is artificial — in a real inference pipeline, multiple layers would run on GPU without sync. Estimated SVM overhead: 2-4 ms per iteration.

### The Fundamental Architecture Problem

The nntrainer kernel uses a **cooperative processing model** (128 work-items process 4 Q rows together with barriers). This works well on NVIDIA GPUs (hardware-scheduled warps, fast shared memory), but on Adreno:

1. **Barriers are expensive**: Adreno's wavefront scheduling makes barriers costlier
2. **Local memory is shared**: 64 KB shared across all running WGs, limiting occupancy to 3 WGs/CU
3. **Sub-group support is recent**: `cl_qcom_subgroups` compiler may not optimize as aggressively

The alternative — **per-WI architecture** (FlashAttention-v2 style, each work-item handles 1 Q row independently) — was tested and was **15.7× slower** (520 ms vs 33 ms) due to register pressure and poor memory coalescing on Adreno.

**Neither cooperative nor per-WI architectures match CPU efficiency on Adreno for this workload.**

### Performance comparision

| Mode | llama.cpp CPU | nntrainer OpenCL | llama.cpp OpenCL (#21313) | nntrainer CPU (#3893) | nntrainer CPU (1T) | **LiteRT GPU FP32** | **LiteRT CPU** |
|------|-------------|-----------------|--------------------------|---------------------|-------------------|---------------------|----------------|
| Prefill 512×512 | 9.24 | 32.0 | 49.44 | 216.0 | 687.0 | **16.006** | 20.328 |
| Decode 1×512 | 0.09 | 1.68 | 0.32 | 0.60 | 1.30 | 2.082 | **0.995** |
---
